_meta.description: Document-rules config for legal_notice_trademark_infringement — cease & desist notice under Trade Marks Act, 1999
_meta.change_protocol: All edits require CLO sign-off. Verify trademark registration certificate and class before issuing infringement notice.

displayName: Legal Notice — Trademark Infringement / Passing Off (Cease & Desist)

trademark.note: If unregistered, proceed on passing-off basis with proof of prior user and goodwill

mandatoryClauses.name: Proprietorship of Trademark
mandatoryClauses.description: Establish ownership — registration number, class, date of registration, date of user; or unregistered prior user for passing off

mandatoryClauses.name: Goodwill & Reputation
mandatoryClauses.description: Reputation accrued through long, continuous, and extensive use; sales figures, advertising spend, market reach

mandatoryClauses.name: Particulars of Infringement
mandatoryClauses.description: Identify infringing mark, products/services, medium of use, similarity (visual/phonetic/conceptual), and likelihood of confusion

mandatoryClauses.name: Statutory Basis
mandatoryClauses.description: Sections 28 (rights of registered proprietor), 29 (infringement), 134 (jurisdiction), 135 (relief) of Trade Marks Act, 1999

mandatoryClauses.name: Cease & Desist Demand
mandatoryClauses.description: Immediate cessation of use, removal of listings, recall and delivery up of infringing goods, destruction of materials

mandatoryClauses.name: Damages / Account of Profits
mandatoryClauses.description: Claim for damages or account of profits at proprietor's election

mandatoryClauses.name: Written Undertaking
mandatoryClauses.description: Demand for written undertaking not to repeat the infringement, supported by affidavit

mandatoryClauses.name: Advocate Details
mandatoryClauses.description: Name and BCI enrollment number of advocate

filingChecklist: Notice sent by Registered Post AD / Speed Post AD
Also serve by email and courier (especially for time-sensitive online infringements)
Postal receipts, AD card, and delivery proof preserved
Trademark Registration Certificate / TM Renewal Certificate annexed
Evidence of prior, continuous, and extensive user preserved — sales invoices, advertising material, third-party recognition
Screenshots and archived copies of infringing online use (with timestamps via archive.org or notarised) preserved before issuing notice
Physical samples of infringing goods preserved with chain of custody
Suit for infringement / passing off under Section 134 — can be filed where proprietor resides or carries on business (additional forum beyond defendant's place)
Consider parallel applications: rectification of trade marks register (if infringer has separate registration), customs notice for IPR enforcement, takedown to platforms under intermediary rules

sections.description: Rights conferred by registration of trademark
Limits on effect of registered trademark
Penalty for applying false trademarks, trade descriptions, etc.
Penalty for selling goods or providing services to which false trademark or false trade description applied
Enhanced penalty on second or subsequent conviction
Suit for infringement — jurisdiction extended to where plaintiff resides or carries on business
Relief in suits for infringement or for passing off — injunction, damages, account of profits, delivery up
Intermediary liability — basis for online takedown demand to platforms
Pre-Institution Mediation — mandatory unless urgent interim relief is sought (IP suits routinely seek injunction so this is generally excluded)

validation_rules.description: Either valid registration certificate OR demonstrable prior user (for passing off) must be established
Infringing goods/services should fall within same/cognate class for infringement; for dissimilar goods, S.29(4) cross-class protection requires reputation
Trademark cease & desist typically allows 7-15 days; no statutory cooling-off but reasonable opportunity recommended
Capture infringement evidence (screenshots, samples) BEFORE issuing notice; addressee will likely modify on receiving notice

promptInstructions: Draft a Cease & Desist Legal Notice for Trademark Infringement under the Trade Marks Act, 1999.

Establish my client's proprietorship — registration number, class (NICE classification), date of registration, date of user, goods/services covered. If unregistered, base notice on passing off and prove prior user + goodwill + misrepresentation + damage.
Set out goodwill — duration of use, sales figures, advertising spend, market presence.
Particularise the infringement — exact infringing mark, products/services on which it is used, channels (offline/online), date of first detection, evidence preserved.
Analyse similarity — visual, phonetic, structural, conceptual — and likelihood of confusion / association.

Demand: (a) immediate cease and desist, (b) recall and delivery up of infringing goods, (c) destruction of packaging and marketing material, (d) removal of online listings, (e) account of profits or damages at proprietor's election, (f) written undertaking on affidavit, (g) costs.
State that on default, suit for permanent injunction with prayer for interim and ex-parte ad-interim orders will be filed in the competent court (HC or Commercial Court) under S.134.
Reserve right to approach customs for IPR enforcement and platforms for intermediary takedown.
Allow 7-15 days response — keep window tight for IP matters; reservation of right to seek ex parte injunction if continued use.
Use firm and assertive legal language.
Do NOT generate the advocate signature block — it is added programmatically.
